newsitem.title: INDIA: Clinton expected to visit India in 1998 - Gujral.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to visit India in 1998 - Gujral.

text.p: President Bill Clinton plans to visit India next year, the first U.S. leader to travel to the South Asian nation since Jimmy Carter in 1978, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Monday.
Gujral told CNN television in an interview that Clinton had accepted his invitation to visit India during year-long celebrations following the 50th anniversary of independence on August 15.
"I have invited President Clinton to visit us in this golden jubilee year. He is most welcome whenever he wants to come," the Indian leader said.
Asked if Clinton had responded to the invitation, Gujral said, "The response is positive, and, whatever, I gather he will be visiting us in the calendar year of 1998."

Indian Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao visited the United States in 1994. U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton came to India in 1995, and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is expected to visit before the end of 1997.
Jimmy Carter, who visited India in early January 1978, was the last U.S. president to come to India.
Gujral was asked if he felt Washington paid little attention politically to India.
"Sometimes it is very interesting for us to see how American policymakers think of Asia as a whole," he said.
"Although we would like to be friendly with the United States, it is for them to take notice of the level."
During the Cold War, ties between Washington and New Delhi were strained as India, while officially non-aligned, nurtured a strong military and economic relationship with Moscow.

But since the breakup of the Soviet Union and the launching of free-market reforms in India in 1991, the United States and India have strengthened links. The United States is India's largest trading partner and investor.
India is waiting for Washington to send an ambassador to New Delhi to replace Frank Wisner, who quit the diplomatic corps for the private sector last month.
